Monica / Stephanie —

Thanks for the snapshot. Technical notes and constraints below:

1) Node mix & equivalence: our A100-80GB-equivalent pool is a mix of 24x A100p nodes (native) and a series of higher-density A100-40GB + software-level aggregation. For strict latency SLAs, prefer native A100p nodes.

2) Mapping for requested 36 GPUs: we can map to 36 native slots by combining 22 nodes in US-west + 14 nodes in US-east. If the customer requires single-region locality, we can do West-only but would consume ~40% of west spare capacity and trigger a soft admission control.

3) Maintenance windows: the 12 nodes flagged in the west can either be deferred (ops change window) or we place them outside the hold; deferring requires a one-time maintenance waiver (no impact to broader schedule, ops will sign off).

4) Proposed soft hold: SOFTHOLD-548-LUM — reserves 36 slots for 21 days starting when we flip the activation toggle. Internal behavior: reserved nodes will be marked DRAIN_SAFE=false for other long-running reservations; ephemeral bursts allowed with admin approval.

5) Headroom and safety: recommend packaging the customer for a 1.1x headroom (reserve 40 slots) so scheduling jitter/burst doesn't starve other commitments. This will be a policy exception documented in the hold request ticket.

I'll prepare the node mapping diagram and a short runbook for activation/rollback; putting a prelim ticket in Jira: SUP-8672 (ops/infra queue).

-Aditya
Principal Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
